name: Dirty Pipe (CVE-2022-0847)
description: Dirty Pipe lets an unprivileged user overwrite read-only files (page cache) on kernels 5.8-5.17. exploit-1 rewrites /etc/passwd to set a root password; exploit-2 hijacks a chosen SUID binary to pop a root shell.

steps.label: 1. Check kernel + build
steps.command:
uname -r   # 5.8 - 5.17 = vulnerable
git clone https://github.com/AlexisAhmed/CVE-2022-0847-DirtyPipe-Exploits.git && cd CVE-2022-0847-DirtyPipe-Exploits && bash compile.sh

defense.why_it_works: Dirty Pipe (CVE-2022-0847) exploits a flaw in the Linux pipe subsystem: a pipe buffer flag (PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE) can be set on a page cache entry of a read-only file via splice(), allowing writes to pages backed by read-only files. This enables overwriting the content of arbitrary read-only files -- including SUID binaries or /etc/passwd -- without write permission.
defense.prerequisites: Linux kernel 5.8 through 5.17 (inclusive). Local user account on the target. Ability to execute compiled C code.
defense.impact: Local privilege escalation to root. Exploit-1 modifies /etc/passwd to set root password to 'piped'. Exploit-2 hijacks any SUID binary to drop a root shell.
defense.detection: Kernel exploit execution generates unusual pipe + splice() syscall patterns. EDR: process writing to read-only file via pipe (anomalous write to /etc/passwd, SUID binary). Auditd: write on /etc/passwd or SUID binaries by non-root. Kernel version check in security monitoring.
defense.artifacts: Auditd: write to /etc/passwd or SUID binary by non-root user | EDR: unusual splice/pipe syscall sequence | /tmp/passwd.bak or /tmp/sh created by exploit
defense.prevention: Patch kernel to 5.16.11+, 5.15.25+, or 5.10.102+. Apply vendor security updates immediately. Use security-hardened kernels (grsecurity, KSPP). Deploy EDR with kernel exploit detection (unusual file writes to read-only files).
defense.misconfiguration: System running Linux kernel 5.8-5.17 without the Dirty Pipe patch applied. Kernel auto-update is disabled or delayed.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Vulnerable kernel version
uname -r
# Output: 5.13.0-xx  <- affected range 5.8-5.17

# No automatic kernel patching configured
defense.secure_config:
# Update kernel (Ubuntu/Debian)
apt update && apt upgrade linux-image-generic

# Verify patched version
uname -r  # should be >= 5.16.11 / 5.15.25 / 5.10.102

# Enable automatic security updates
apt install unattended-upgrades
dpkg-reconfigure unattended-upgrades
